english.title: Onwardly disclose personal information disclosed under sections 35 - 39
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) having received personal information **(..GIVE DETAILS OF INFORMATION..), that was disclosed under sections 35 to 39 of the Digital Economy Act 2017, onwardly disclosed that information, knowing or being reckless as to whether the disclosure was unlawful
english.legislation: Contrary to section 41 of the Digital Economy Act 2017.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being a person in receipt of personal information disclosed under sections 35 to 39 of the Digital Economy Act
onwardly disclose that information
knowing this disclosure was unlawful and/or being reckless as to whether the disclosure was unlawful

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This section does not apply to personal information disclosed under sections 35, 36 or 38 of the Digital Economy Act 2017 by Revenue and Customs - see for details of this offence.
(ii) See section 41(2) of that Act which gives information whereby disclosure would not constitute an offence, examples being onward disclosure for the purposes of prevention or detection of crime, disclosure in pursuance of a court order etc.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 41(7) of the Digital Economy Act 2017 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
Time limit for prosecutions:
None
